allergies: ALL tree nuts EXCEPT pistachio and chestnut (both safe)
finned fish (salmon, tuna, cod, etc.) AND fish oil — including supplements/softgels and fish-oil-fortified products (some milks, juices, 'omega-3' foods). Shellfish IS safe

legumes: beans, peas, chickpeas, lentils — EXCEPT whole soy (tofu, edamame), which is safe. Watch for hidden pea protein / chickpea flour / lentil flour in protein powders, bars, pastas, and 'high-protein' products
avocado (the fruit) — refined avocado OIL is tolerated and fine
bell peppers — SPECIFICALLY bell peppers: jalapeños, chilis, cayenne, paprika, hot sauce, and salsa are all safe
avoid: soy protein isolate/concentrate (common in protein powders and bars) — questionable, not confirmed; whole soy like tofu and edamame is fine
Fairlife Nutrition Plan shakes — Adam doesn't digest them well (10/4/2026). Not an allergy; just don't plan them
diet.sharedKitchen: Adam shares the kitchen — items in the home (almond milk, nut pesto, walnut snacks) may belong to others. Never infer safety from kitchen contents; only profile.diet governs. Cross-contact awareness applies to shared surfaces/utensils.
diet.note: Everything in allergies is a medical allergy: when curating data/foods.json (docs/foods.md) or suggesting any food, check 'may contain' / shared-facility warnings for ALL allergy entries — not just ingredient lists. Pea protein is the biggest hidden risk in fitness foods. The avoid list is ingredient-level only.

supplements.name: Creatine monohydrate
supplements.note: Maintenance dose, no loading phase. Timing irrelevant (saturation-based) - consistency is the only thing that matters. Adds ~1-2 lb of intracellular water over the first 1-3 weeks: weigh-ins from 2026-08-21 through ~2026-09-05 are confounded and must not be used for the TDEE recompute.

supplements.name: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol), Nature Made tablets
supplements.note: Ordered 9/20/2026 in response to the 9/15 Rythm panel: vitamin D 34.5 ng/mL (ref 30-80), essentially flat from 35.0 on 8/07 across an entire summer. Target band 40-60. Adam takes it alongside the daily creatine. TABLET form and LANOLIN-sourced, deliberately: D3 is commonly derived from cod liver oil and softgels often use fish gelatin, both of which his finned-fish/fish-oil allergy rules out. USP Verified. FAT-SOLUBLE - absorption is meaningfully better with a fat-containing meal, so anchor the creatine+D3 pair to dinner rather than an empty stomach. EXPECT the next panel to show D rising ~10-15 ng/mL; that is the supplement working, not a lab anomaly. UPDATE 10/10: the 10/8 panel read 26.8 (DOWN from 34.5) only ~2.5 weeks in, with Adam taking it ~80% of days. Too early to judge (D3 takes ~2-3 months to plateau) and the season is working against it; the fix is consistency (keep it with the creatine at dinner), not a dose change. Judge the December panel: still <30 means ask a doctor about a higher dose. UPDATE 11/11: the 11/8 panel read 33.6 (up from 26.8), so it is moving the right way. Keep the dose and the dinner habit, and judge it on the December panel.

supplements.name: Magnesium glycinate (bisglycinate)
supplements.note: Started 11/14/2026 at Adam's request, for sleep. Dose is ELEMENTAL magnesium (labels also print total glycinate weight, which is much larger); keep supplemental Mg under the 350 mg/day UL. Take 30-60 min before bed, separate from the dinner creatine+D3 pair (no interaction, just different anchors). Expect at most a modest effect: the evidence is strongest in people who are low, magnesium has not been measured on any panel, and the real sleep problem as of Nov 2026 is late lights-out (several nights after 2am), which a supplement does not fix. Plain bisglycinate only; no sleep blends with melatonin/ashwagandha/herbs. Allergy-check the label like any packaged product.
